tool_input.body:
Closes ethos-i1z8, ethos-21v0.

Two fixes found while closing out cluster 3, done here rather than deferred to beads.

## 1. `ethos mission result` silently accepted YAML-comment-truncated values

This bit us for real on PR #516. A result file contained:

```yaml
- name: PR #515 merged as 6f61406 — 6/6 CI checks green, 17 review threads resolved
  status: pass
```

YAML treats an unquoted ` #` as a start-of-comment, so the parsed name was `PR`. Validation only required a non-empty name, and `"PR"` is non-empty — so it passed, was written to `results.yaml`, and round-tripped through `ethos mission close` with `status: pass` intact. A record asserting success about something it no longer described.

**Mechanism, not a heuristic.** yaml.v3 hands back the discarded text as the node's `LineComment`, so a truncated scalar is exactly one that is *plain* and *carries a line comment*. Quoted and block scalars are excluded by style. A length rule would have rejected `make check` and missed a long value cut at character 40.

**Fixed as a class.** All four submitted-artifact schemas had the same exposure: results (`evidence[].name`, `open_questions`, plain `prose`), reflections (`reason`, `signals`), corrections (`claim`, `corrected`, `evidence[].name`), and contracts (`success_criteria`, `context`, `delegations[].message`). Corrections are the sharpest case — the artifact that retracts a false claim about a PR would itself be cut at that PR's number.

Block scalars need no special-casing: `prose: |` has no comment syntax, so `#` there is content and yaml.v3 attaches no `LineComment`. Plain single-line `prose` *is* checked, because there the comment syntax is live.

Contracts get the check at the three entry points where a human's file arrives rather than inside `DecodeContractStrict`, which also reads contracts back off disk — marshalled bytes carry no comments, so a rejection on that path could never help.

## 2. `internal/repomiss` had no tests

97 lines, zero test files, so it produced no `ok` line and reported 0.0% coverage — while being the dependency-free leaf shared by the four layered stores (which produce misses) and `internal/vendor`/`internal/doctor` (which verify completeness). Now 100.0% of statements, with `repomiss.go` unchanged; no defect was found in it.

The copy property in `Sorted` is pinned twice, since it is invisible without a test and the most likely casualty of a future "optimization". The stability claim in its doc comment is proved rather than asserted: all six permutations of the same three misses produce a byte-identical `Error()`.

## Verification

Both gates falsified, not just observed passing.

Truncation, pre-fix red on the exact PR #516 line:

```
--- FAIL: TestDecodeResultRejectsHashTruncatedEvidenceName
    submission accepted; evidence name parsed as "PR"
--- FAIL: TestDecodeResultRejectsHashTruncatedOpenQuestion
--- FAIL: TestDecodeResultRejectsHashTruncatedPlainProse
--- FAIL: TestDecodeReflectionRejectsHashTruncation/reason
```

`Sorted`'s copy guard, falsified by replacing `append([]MissingRef(nil), refs...)` with `out := refs`:

```
--- FAIL: TestNewDoesNotMutateCaller
--- FAIL: TestSortedReturnsACopy
```

Driven through the real binary, not only in-process:

```
$ .tmp/ethos-verify mission result m-2026-09-10-001 --file .tmp/trunc-test.yaml
ethos: mission result: invalid result: evidence[0].name: value truncated at an
unquoted '#': YAML kept "PR" from line 8 (- name: PR #515 merged as 6f61406 —
6/6 CI checks green); quote the value, or move the comment to its own line

$ # same file, name quoted:
ethos: mission result: mission "m-2026-09-10-001" is in terminal state "closed"
```

The quoted form clears the new check and reaches the real gate.

`make check` green with race: **29 ok, 0 FAIL** (up from 28 — `repomiss` now emits an `ok` line). `internal/repomiss` 100.0%, `internal/mission` 85.1%.

## Note on ethos-21v0

That bead also named `tests/behavioral` as reporting 0.0%. That is **not** a defect and is unchanged here — every file there is behind `//go:build behavioral` and needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` plus the `claude` CLI, so without the tag the package has no files. The bead was filed on a misread of the build tag.

tool_input.message:
PR #517 is up with your two commits; all CI green. Eight review findings landed from qodo, Cursor Bugbot, and Copilot. I verified the two most serious myself before sending. Fix these in this PR — do not file follow-up beads for any of them.

**1. `contractHashScope` points at a field that does not exist, and misses the one that does.** (qodo #1, Bugbot, Copilot — three reviewers independently.) Verified by reading the structs: `DelegationTemplate` (`internal/mission/delegation.go:74`) has `Role`, `SpawnPattern`, `InheritsContract`, `ExtractInto` — no `message`. `Precondition` (`internal/mission/mission.go:188`) *does* have `Message`. So `record: map[string]string{"delegations": "message"}` at `hashtrunc.go:80` guards nothing — `KnownFields` would reject that key before the walk fires — while `preconditions[].message`, a real human-authored gate-denial string, is unprotected. Copilot also names `inputs.trigger.subject`; verify whether that field exists and is free text, and cover it if so.

Point the scope at `preconditions`, drop the nonexistent path, and add regression cases proving a truncated `preconditions[].message` is rejected. The scope model may need nested-record support — qodo says so; judge it against the real schema rather than taking its word.

**2. The CHANGELOG repeats the same false claim.** It advertises `delegations[].message` coverage. That is my error — I wrote it into the PR description too and did not check it. Correct it to name the fields actually covered. An entry that overstates what a guard protects is the exact defect class this PR exists to close, so it does not get to ship inside the fix for it.

**3. `files_changed[].path` is excluded from the check, but paths permit `#`.** (Copilot.) Confirmed by running the real binary, not by reading: a result with `path: reports/PR #515.txt` passed the truncation guard entirely and reached the mission-state gate. `validateWriteSetEntry` rejects null bytes, colons, drive letters, and traversal — not spaces or `#` — so the path silently becomes `reports/PR` and can still satisfy write-set containment, persisting a different file than the worker declared. Either include path-bearing fields in the check or reject the syntax explicitly; do not leave paths treated as "constrained enough."

**4. `prose: # no narrative` is rejected as truncated.** (qodo #2.) A plain scalar with an empty parsed value plus a line comment is not truncation — it is an intentional comment on an omitted optional field. Verify `Result.Prose` is genuinely optional, then treat an empty parsed value as non-truncated and let normal schema validation handle required-but-empty. Add the regression case. This is the false-positive class I flagged as most likely when I opened the PR, so I want it closed properly rather than argued away.

**5. Aliases and YAML merge keys bypass the guard.** (qodo #3.) The traversal inspects direct scalar nodes only, while typed decoding resolves `*alias` and `<<` into the checked fields — so an anchored truncated scalar reaches a field without inspection. Verify this is actually reachable before building anything; if it is, prefer rejecting aliases and merge keys outright in submitted mission artifacts over writing a resolver, unless you can show the resolver is genuinely simple. Say which you chose and why.

**6. A test can pass while the implementation is broken.** (Copilot, `cmd/ethos/mission_hashtrunc_test.go:97`.) It skips both assertions when `loadErr != nil`, so an implementation that writes an unreadable result still satisfies it. Require the load to succeed, then assert. Check the rest of the new tests for the same shape — a conditional that turns a failure into a skip is the same defect one level up, and we have already had five tests on an earlier branch that guarded their own fixtures.

Verify each finding against source before acting; two reviewers have been wrong earlier in this session and being wrong is itself worth reporting. Every fix confirmed red against pre-fix code with output pasted. `make check` green with race, both counts. Do not push — report and I push.
